title: Spiced Saudi-Style Chicken and Rice with Tomato, Almonds and Raisins
summary: Saudi-style kabsa: chicken pieces browned and then simmered on fragrant basmati rice cooked with tomato, carrot, warm spices and dried lime. Finished with toasted almonds, pine nuts and plump golden raisins.
equipment: large heavy casserole with a lid (5-6 litres)
wire rack set over a baking tray (optional, for grilling)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dried lime (loomi), pierced, or a 7 cm strip of lime peel
basmati rice, rinsed until the water runs almost clear
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Salt the chicken
steps.text: Pat the chicken dry and rub it all over with the 0.75 tsp salt. Leave it for 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 8 hours uncovered in the fridge. Early salting seasons the meat more deeply and dries the skin so it browns better.

steps.title: Brown in batches
steps.text: Heat the oil in the casserole over medium-high heat and brown the chicken skin side down in 2 batches, 5-7 minutes per batch, until golden; lower the heat if it smokes. Set the pieces aside on the plate. Working in batches stops the pan cooling, so the skin sears instead of steaming.

steps.title: Build the spice base
steps.text: Pour off all but 2 tbsp of the fat and cook the onion over medium heat for 5 minutes until lightly golden. Add the garlic, ginger, tomato paste, all the ground spices, pepper and cardamom and stir for 1 minute until fragrant. Frying the spices and paste in the fat deepens their flavour and removes the raw edge of the tomato.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the tomatoes, carrot, bay leaves and dried lime and cook for 4 minutes, scraping up the browned bits from the base, until thick and jammy. Those caramelised bits dissolve into the sauce and give the rice its savoury depth.

steps.title: Toast the rice
steps.text: Tip in the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the edges of the grains turn translucent. Coating the grains in the spiced fat helps them stay separate and absorb the flavour evenly.

steps.title: Simmer with chicken
steps.text: Stir in the water and the 0.5 tsp salt, nestle in the chicken skin side up with any juices and bring to the boil. Cover, turn the heat to medium-low and simmer gently for 25-30 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed. Check the thickest thigh next to the bone: it must read 74 °C; if it does not, lift out the chicken, cover the rice and grill the chicken on the rack under a hot grill (broiler) for 4-5 minutes until it reaches 74 °C.

steps.title: Rest and crisp
steps.text: Lift out the chicken, fluff the rice gently with a fork and discard the cardamom, bay leaves and lime, then cover and rest off the heat for 10 minutes. For crisper skin, grill the chicken on the rack for 2-3 minutes until spotted brown while the rice rests. Resting lets the steam finish softening the grains.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.text: Fry the almonds and pine nuts in the olive oil in the small frying pan over medium-low heat for 2-3 minutes until golden, then add the raisins for 30 seconds until plump. Pile the rice onto a platter, arrange the chicken on top and scatter over the nut and raisin topping.

tips: A common mistake is lifting the lid to check the rice; keep it closed so the steam does its work and the grains cook evenly.
Pierce the dried lime before adding it so its tangy, slightly smoky flavour seeps into the rice; a strip of lime peel works if you cannot find loomi.
Always check the chicken next to the bone, as the meat there is the last to reach 74 °C.
Add the raisins to the hot oil only briefly; any longer and they scorch and turn bitter.
storage: Cool quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour and use within 24 hours. Reheat once, covered, until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
